steps: Plot points using correct scales on both axes
Look at the pattern: up, down, or scattered
Name it: positive, negative, or no correlation
Draw a best-fit line through the middle
Use the line to estimate values; spot anomalies
method_card.title: Scatter Graphs & Correlation
method_card.content:
A scatter graph (scatter diagram) plots two variables against each other to see if there is a relationship (correlation) between them. One variable goes on each axis — typically the independent variable (cause) on the x-axis and the dependent variable (effect) on the y-axis.

Positive correlation: As one variable increases, the other increases. Points slope upward from left to right (e.g. GDP and life expectancy).

Negative correlation: As one variable increases, the other decreases. Points slope downward (e.g. altitude and temperature).

No correlation: No clear pattern — the points are randomly scattered.

Line of best fit: A straight line drawn through the middle of the points, with roughly equal numbers of points above and below. It should follow the trend of the data and can be used to estimate (interpolate) values. Extrapolation (predicting beyond the data range) is less reliable.

Anomalies (outliers) are points that don't fit the general pattern. In geography, these often have interesting explanations — for example, a country with high GDP but low life expectancy might be affected by conflict.
method_card.example:
Question: A scatter graph shows GDP per capita ($) on the x-axis and life expectancy (years) on the y-axis for 15 countries. The points slope upwards from left to right. What type of correlation is this?

Step 1: As GDP increases (left to right), life expectancy also increases (bottom to top).

Step 2: Both variables increase together → positive correlation.

Step 3: This suggests that wealthier countries tend to have higher life expectancy.

gold.display: The scatter graph shows GDP per capita and CO₂ emissions for 12 countries. Describe the correlation and explain why one country (top-right point) is an anomaly.
options: Strong positive correlation. The anomaly has extremely high per-capita emissions due to its oil/gas economy and small population.
Weak positive correlation. The anomaly fits the general trend.
Strong negative correlation. The anomaly has low emissions.
No correlation. All countries produce similar emissions.

misconceptions.message: Most points show strong positive correlation. The top-right point (65000, 35) is far above the trend — likely a petro-state with a small population, creating disproportionately high per-capita emissions.

gold.display: A student plots rainfall vs crop yield and uses the line to predict yield at 1200mm when data only goes to 800mm. Why is this unreliable?
options: 1200mm is outside the data range (extrapolation) — too much rain may flood crops, reversing the trend
The line of best fit is always wrong
You can only interpolate with negative correlation
1200mm is impossible in the UK

misconceptions.message: Extrapolating to 1200mm goes far beyond the data (max 800mm). The positive relationship may not continue — excessive rainfall could damage crops, creating a different pattern.

gold.display: The scatter graph shows literacy rate (%) and birth rate (per 1000). The correlation coefficient is -0.92. What does this value tell us?
options: Strong negative correlation — as literacy increases, birth rate decreases significantly
Weak negative correlation — slight relationship
Strong positive correlation — both increase together
The value proves literacy causes lower birth rates

misconceptions.message: Correlation does NOT prove causation! -0.92 shows strong negative correlation (close to -1), but other factors like healthcare, education for women, and contraception also play a role.

gold.display: Two students draw different lines of best fit. Student A's line has 5 points above and 5 below. Student B's line passes through the first and last points. Whose is more appropriate?
options: Student A — a good line of best fit has roughly equal points above and below
Student B — the line should connect the endpoints
Both are equally valid
Neither — the line must pass through the origin

misconceptions.message: A line of best fit should pass through the 'middle' of the data with roughly equal points on each side. It does NOT need to pass through any specific points or the origin.

gold.hint: Interpolate between the points at 40° and 50°.
gold.display: The scatter graph shows distance from the equator and daylight variation. Estimate the variation at 45° latitude.

misconceptions.message: At 40° = 7 hours, at 50° = 10 hours. Midpoint (45°) ≈ 8.5 hours, rounded to 9.

bronze.display: The scatter graph shows GDP per capita and life expectancy for 10 countries. What type of correlation does the graph show?
options: Positive correlation
Negative correlation
No correlation
Perfect correlation

misconceptions.message: As GDP increases, life expectancy also increases — points slope upward from left to right. This is positive correlation.

bronze.display: A scatter graph shows altitude (m) on the x-axis and temperature (°C) on the y-axis. Points slope downward from left to right. What type of correlation is this?
options: Positive correlation
Negative correlation
No correlation
Cannot determine

misconceptions.message: Points sloping downward = as one variable increases, the other decreases. This is negative correlation.

bronze.display: The scatter graph shows temperature and ice cream sales. Which point is most likely an anomaly?
options: Point at 25°C, 300 sales
Point at 30°C, 50 sales
Point at 15°C, 100 sales
Point at 20°C, 200 sales

misconceptions.message: The general trend is positive (higher temp → more sales). The point at 30°C with only 50 sales is far below the trend — it's an anomaly (perhaps it rained that day).

bronze.display: The scatter graph shows distance from the city centre and house prices. What type of correlation is shown?
options: Positive correlation
Negative correlation
No correlation
Strong positive correlation

misconceptions.message: As distance increases, house price decreases. Points slope downward = negative correlation.

bronze.display: A scatter graph compares hours of sunshine and number of tourists at a beach resort. As sunshine increases, tourist numbers increase. Describe the relationship.
options: Positive correlation — more sunshine attracts more tourists
Negative correlation — more sunshine reduces tourist numbers
No correlation — sunshine doesn't affect tourism
Positive correlation — tourists cause more sunshine

misconceptions.message: Careful! While the correlation is positive, tourists don't cause sunshine. Sunshine is the independent variable that influences tourism.

bronze.hint: Estimate where x = 40 would fall on the trend line.
bronze.display: The scatter graph shows rainfall and river discharge. Using the graph, estimate the discharge when rainfall is 40mm.

misconceptions.message: The trend suggests about 0.44 cumecs per mm of rainfall. At 40mm, estimate about 18 cumecs (between 35mm=16 and 45mm=20).

bronze.display: Which of these pairs of geographical variables would you expect to show NO correlation?
options: Rainfall and river discharge
Population density and distance from capital
Shoe size and rainfall
Temperature and altitude

misconceptions.message: Shoe size and rainfall have no logical connection. The other pairs all have clear geographical relationships.

bronze.display: The scatter graph shows development indicators for 8 countries. How many countries have both GDP above $20,000 and life expectancy above 75 years?

silver.display: The scatter graph shows distance from the sea and annual temperature range. Describe the correlation and explain it geographically.
options: Positive — the sea has a moderating effect, so inland areas have greater temperature range
Negative — further from the sea means cooler temperatures overall
No correlation — the sea doesn't affect temperature range
Positive — coastal areas have the greatest temperature range

misconceptions.message: Positive correlation. The sea heats/cools slowly (high specific heat capacity), moderating coastal temperatures. Inland areas lack this effect, giving larger temperature ranges.

silver.hint: Find 25 on the x-axis and estimate where the trend line would cross.
silver.display: The scatter graph shows birth rate and infant mortality for 10 countries. Using the line of best fit, estimate the infant mortality rate for a country with a birth rate of 25.

misconceptions.message: At birth rate 25, the trend suggests approximately 40 per 1000 infant mortality (between the points at 22→32 and 28→45).

silver.display: A scatter graph shows HDI vs CO₂ emissions with strong positive correlation. One country with HDI 0.85 has very low emissions. Why might it be an anomaly?
options: Data entry error — the point should be deleted
The country may rely heavily on renewable energy despite high development
The country has a very large population diluting emissions
HDI and CO₂ have no relationship

misconceptions.message: A highly developed country with low emissions likely uses clean energy (e.g. Norway, Iceland use hydropower/geothermal). Anomalies often have real geographical explanations.

silver.display: The scatter graph shows distance downstream and river velocity. What type of correlation is shown, and what does it suggest?
options: Positive — rivers flow faster downstream as tributaries add water and the channel becomes more efficient
Negative — rivers slow down as they approach the sea
No correlation — velocity is random along a river
Positive — rivers flow faster downstream due to steeper gradients

misconceptions.message: Gradient actually decreases downstream! Velocity increases because the channel becomes wider and deeper (more efficient), and tributaries add water volume.
Clear upward trend = positive correlation. Rivers speed up downstream as channel efficiency increases.

silver.display: A scatter graph of population density vs distance from CBD shows negative correlation. One point at 3km from CBD has unusually low density. Suggest a geographical explanation.
options: It could be a park, industrial zone or transport hub with few residents
The data must be wrong
3km is too close to the CBD for anyone to live
Negative correlation means all nearby areas have low density

misconceptions.message: Near the CBD, land use isn't all residential — parks, railway stations, or industrial estates would show low population density despite being close to the centre.

silver.display: The scatter graph shows latitude and average annual temperature. Using the graph, estimate the temperature at latitude 35°N.

misconceptions.message: At 35°N, interpolate between 30°N (20°C) and 40°N (15°C). Midpoint ≈ 17.5°C, so approximately 18°C.

silver.display: Why is extrapolation from a scatter graph less reliable than interpolation?
options: Extrapolation predicts beyond the data range where the pattern may not continue
Extrapolation can only be done with negative correlation
Interpolation uses a wider range of data
Extrapolation is always wrong

misconceptions.message: Extrapolation goes beyond the collected data. The trend may change outside the measured range, making predictions less reliable.

steps.label: Identify correlation type
steps.content: Positive correlation — as rainfall increases, river discharge increases.

steps.label: Explain geographically
steps.content: More rainfall means more water entering the river through surface runoff and throughflow, increasing the volume of water (discharge) in the river channel.

worked_examples.question: A scatter graph plots rainfall (mm) against river discharge (cumecs). The points show a clear upward trend. Describe the correlation and suggest a reason.

steps.label: Read from line of best fit
steps.content: Draw a vertical line up to the line of best fit, then read across to the y-axis.

steps.label: State the estimate
steps.content: The line of best fit crosses at approximately 72 years. This is an interpolation (within the data range) so is reasonably reliable.

worked_examples.question: Use the scatter graph to estimate the life expectancy for a country with GDP per capita of $15,000.
